text: 18-month-old boy. The patient is brought in by his parents due to swelling in his right knee noticed after playing in the park. The parents report that there was no obvious injury or incident at the park that could have led to the swelling. Upon further questioning, the mother recalls that an uncle on her side of the family had similar problems, suggesting a possible genetic component.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Is the knee red, warm to the touch, or particularly painful when he moves it? Also, has he had any episodes of bleeding from other sites, such as nosebleeds or bleeding gums, in the past?

text: The PT is normal, which is consistent with a factor VIII or IX deficiency where only the intrinsic pathway is affected. I need the PTT result to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: PTT

speaker: Doctor
text: A normal PTT makes a diagnosis of hemophilia unlikely, as that condition typically presents with a prolonged partial thromboplastin time. I need to investigate other causes for the knee swelling, such as an inflammatory or infectious process. REQUEST TEST: Knee_Ultrasound
